requirements.title: setup_zsh_plugins.sh installs zsh and three plugins
requirements.body: The module installs zsh via apt if absent, then clones romkatv/powerlevel10k, zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions, and zdharma-continuum/fast-syntax-highlighting into ~/.zsh/plugins/. On subsequent runs it git-pulls each plugin instead of re-cloning.

scenarios.title: Clean slate install
then: zsh is installed via apt
all three plugin directories exist under ~/.zsh/plugins/
the script exits 0

scenarios.title: Idempotent re-run
given: all three plugin directories already exist as git repos
scenarios.when: bash lib/setup_zsh_plugins.sh is run a second time
then: git pull is called on each plugin (no re-clone)
the script exits 0
no duplicate entries appear in ~/.zshrc

requirements.title: Managed block in ~/.zshrc is idempotent
requirements.body: The module writes exactly one OPEN-CHAD ZSH BEGIN/END block to ~/.zshrc. Running the module N times results in exactly one block. User content outside the block is never modified.

scenarios.title: First run appends block
then: ~/.zshrc contains exactly one OPEN-CHAD ZSH BEGIN/END block
all pre-existing user content is preserved verbatim

scenarios.title: Second run does not duplicate block
given: ~/.zshrc already contains an OPEN-CHAD ZSH BEGIN/END block
then: ~/.zshrc still contains exactly one block (count=1), not two

requirements.title: Plugin sourcing order is correct
requirements.body: The managed block sources plugins in the order: powerlevel10k → zsh-autosuggestions → fast-syntax-highlighting. fast-syntax-highlighting must be last.

scenarios.title: Correct plugin order in managed block
scenarios.when: the OPEN-CHAD ZSH BEGIN/END block in ~/.zshrc is inspected
then: powerlevel10k source line appears before zsh-autosuggestions
zsh-autosuggestions appears before fast-syntax-highlighting

requirements.title: --skip-zsh flag skips the wizard step non-interactively
requirements.body: wizard.sh accepts --skip-zsh / SKIP_ZSH=1. install.sh accepts --skip-zsh and passes it through. In --yes mode the chsh prompt is silently skipped.

scenarios.title: Wizard completes without hanging when --skip-zsh is set
given: wizard.sh is invoked with --yes --skip-zsh and all other --skip-* flags
then: it completes in under 10 seconds without hanging
setup_zsh_plugins.sh is not called

requirements.title: open-chad update re-runs setup_zsh_plugins.sh non-fatally
requirements.body: lib/update.sh calls setup_zsh_plugins.sh. If it fails, a warning is emitted but the update continues and exits 0.

scenarios.title: Update continues on zsh setup failure
then: update.sh emits a WARN line
update continues to completion with exit 0

requirements.title: Primary launcher command is openchad with oc alias
requirements.body: Installer and update flows publish openchad as the canonical launcher while providing oc as a forwarding alias. Legacy open-chad usage must be detected and guided with migration messaging rather than silently breaking.

scenarios.title: Fresh install creates canonical and alias launchers
then: ~/.local/bin/openchad exists and points to repo launcher
~/.local/bin/oc exists and forwards all args to openchad
cds, oc-list, and oc-killall symlinks still exist

scenarios.title: Legacy invocation gets migration guidance
given: a user invokes open-chad after the rename
then: the user receives a clear migration warning or compatibility path
documentation and doctor output reference openchad as canonical

requirements.title: Symlink lifecycle is centralized and consistent
requirements.body: All symlink management must be driven by a single manifest consumed by install, update, doctor, uninstall, and installer tests to prevent drift between command sets.

scenarios.title: Install and update use same managed symlink set
given: the managed symlink manifest is defined
scenarios.when: install.sh and lib/update.sh are executed independently
then: both scripts create/repair the exact same symlink names
no command exists in one path but not the other

requirements.title: Rename rollout is TDD-first and regression-tested
requirements.body: For rename and alias behavior, tests are authored before implementation changes and regression coverage spans install, update, shell profile wiring, and oc session helpers.

scenarios.title: Red-to-green ordering is explicit in task graph
given: implementation tasks for launcher rename and aliasing
then: implementation tasks are blocked by the TDD scaffolding task
no test task is blocked by implementation tasks

requirements.title: setup_vision.sh registers 4 MCP servers idempotently
requirements.body: setup_vision.sh verifies the vision binary is on PATH (non-fatal warn if missing), creates ~/.config/vision/servers.yaml with 0600 permissions, and registers context7 (6276), grep-app (6288), lgrep (6285), and firecrawl (6281). Running the script N times results in exactly one entry per server.

scenarios.title: Clean slate install
then: ~/.config/vision/servers.yaml is created with 0600 permissions
all 4 MCP servers are registered (context7, grep-app, lgrep, firecrawl)
the script exits 0

scenarios.title: Idempotent re-run
scenarios.when: bash lib/setup_vision.sh is run a second time
then: no duplicate server entries are added
the script exits 0

scenarios.title: Binary missing is non-fatal
given: vision binary is NOT on PATH
then: a warning is printed mentioning vision
the script exits 0 (non-fatal)

requirements.title: Vision daemon starts as singleton on openchad launch
requirements.body: bin/openchad starts the Vision daemon as a fire-and-forget singleton using a two-tier lock (atomic mkdir vision-start.lock + daemon self-manages PID). vision.log is created with 0600 permissions. A second concurrent openchad launch must not start a second daemon.

scenarios.title: First launch starts daemon
then: vision-start.lock is created atomically
vision daemon start is invoked in the background
$OPEN_CHAD_CACHE_DIR/vision.log is created with 0600 permissions
vision-start.lock is removed after 2 seconds

scenarios.title: Concurrent launch does not duplicate daemon
given: vision-start.lock already exists (another launch in progress)
scenarios.when: a second openchad is launched concurrently
then: the second launch skips daemon start (mkdir fails)
exactly one Vision daemon process runs

requirements.title: openchad doctor reports Vision health
requirements.body: openchad doctor checks: vision binary on PATH, vision daemon status, and all 4 MCP ports reachable via curl with a 2-second timeout. Missing binary or unreachable ports cause a non-zero exit.

scenarios.title: All healthy
given: all 4 MCP ports respond within 2 seconds
then: all Vision checks pass
the script exits 0

scenarios.title: Binary missing causes failure
given: vision binary is NOT on PATH
then: doctor reports vision binary missing
the script exits non-zero

requirements.title: Vision daemon is stopped on uninstall
requirements.body: openchad_uninstall.sh stops the Vision daemon before removing symlinks. The stop is non-fatal if Vision is not installed or not running.

scenarios.title: Daemon running at uninstall time
then: vision daemon stop is called before symlink removal
the script exits 0

scenarios.title: Binary missing is non-fatal at uninstall
given: vision binary is NOT on PATH
then: daemon stop is skipped gracefully
the script exits 0

requirements.title: ADV is installed at a pinned commit SHA by default
requirements.body: setup_adv.sh reads config/opencode/adv-lock.json for the repo URL and pinned commit SHA. The ref field must be a 40-character lowercase hex SHA. Branch names (main, trunk, master, HEAD, develop, dev) and semver tags (v1.2.3) are rejected with a WARN and the script falls back to bundled command docs. The default install mode is 'pinned'.

scenarios.title: Pinned install checks out exact SHA
given: adv-lock.json contains a valid 40-char hex SHA ref
scenarios.when: bash lib/setup_adv.sh is run with ADV_INSTALL_MODE=pinned
then: ADV is cloned or pulled from the repo URL in adv-lock.json
git checkout is called with the exact SHA from adv-lock.json
the script exits 0

scenarios.title: Invalid lock ref falls back to bundled
given: adv-lock.json ref is a branch name like 'main'
then: a WARN is emitted about the invalid ref
bundled command docs are synced to ~/.config/opencode/command/
the script exits 0 (non-fatal)

requirements.title: ADV install has exactly two fallback tiers
requirements.body: The ADV install flow has exactly two tiers: (1) network clone/build at pinned ref, (2) bundled command docs from config/opencode/command/. There is no third tier. Any network or build failure falls back to tier 2 and exits 0. The bundled fallback must contain at least 10 adv-*.md command files.

scenarios.title: Network failure falls back to bundled
given: git clone fails (invalid URL or no network)
scenarios.when: bash lib/setup_adv.sh is run with ADV_INSTALL_MODE=pinned
then: a WARN is emitted about the network failure
bundled command docs are synced to ~/.config/opencode/command/
the script exits 0

scenarios.title: Offline mode skips network entirely
then: no git clone or pull is attempted
bundled command docs are synced to ~/.config/opencode/command/
the script exits 0

scenarios.title: Bundled command docs are present in repo
given: the open-chad repo is checked out
then: at least 10 adv-*.md files are present
core commands exist: adv-status, adv-proposal, adv-apply, adv-archive, adv-prep, adv-research, adv-review, adv-harden

requirements.title: Lock ref is immutable during normal update; --adv-latest opt-in bumps it
requirements.body: openchad update honors the pinned ref from adv-lock.json by default. The lock file is never mutated during a normal update run. Passing --adv-latest to openchad update pulls the latest ADV HEAD and updates adv-lock.json ref to the new commit SHA.

scenarios.title: Normal update uses pinned ref
then: ADV is checked out at the pinned SHA
adv-lock.json is not modified

scenarios.title: --adv-latest pulls latest and bumps lock
then: ADV is pulled to latest HEAD
adv-lock.json ref is updated to the new HEAD SHA
the new ref is a valid 40-char hex SHA

requirements.title: openchad doctor reports ADV health with actionable remediation
requirements.body: openchad doctor checks: adv-lock.json present with valid ref, bundled command docs count >= 10, ADV checkout present (non-fatal if absent), plugin wired in opencode.json, command docs synced to ~/.config/opencode/command/. Each failing check emits an actionable remediation hint.

scenarios.title: All ADV checks pass
given: adv-lock.json present with valid SHA ref
then: all ADV health checks pass
no remediation hints are emitted for ADV

scenarios.title: Missing lock file is reported with remediation
then: doctor reports adv-lock.json missing
remediation hint suggests running bash install.sh
